name: CycloDockDB
description: Disulfide-rich cyclic peptides represent robust structural scaffolds for membrane protein-targeted drug discovery, yet systematic high-throughput structural interaction datasets for human membrane protein targets remain insufficient. Herein, we report CycloDockDB (www.cyclodockdb.cn), an open-access bioinformatics database hosting 68,432 non-redundant molecular docking complexes generated via standardized HADDOCK 3 simulations. The dataset covers 1,602 unique disulfide-rich cyclic peptides across 23 superfamilies and 147 manually curated druggable pockets of human membrane proteins. CycloDockDB archives pre-computed PDB-format docking poses, unified HADDOCK binding scores, decomposed energetic components (van der Waals, electrostatic, and desolvation energies), and buried surface area metrics. Technical validation confirmed reliable internal structural consistency for high-confidence docking clusters (DOCKQ ≥ 0.5). As a dedicated computational benchmark and hypothesis-generating resource, CycloDockDB fills the gap in large-scale structural datasets for cyclic peptide–membrane protein interactions, supporting machine learning model training, algorithm evaluation, and structure-based peptide drug screening.
